# PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS] Contents of this Part

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS] Title | Number

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS] Scope and interpretation | Rule 61.1

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS] Admiralty claims | Rule 61.2

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS] Claims in rem | Rule 61.3

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS] Special provisions relating to collision claims | Rule 61.4

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS] Arrest | Rule 61.5

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS] Security in claim in rem | Rule 61.6

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS] Cautions against arrest | Rule 61.7

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS] Release and cautions against release | Rule 61.8

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS] Judgment in default | Rule 61.9

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS] Sale by the court, priorities and payment out | Rule 61.10

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS] Limitation claims | Rule 61.11

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS] Assessors | Rule 61.13

## Scope and interpretation

## 61.1

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (1) This Part applies to admiralty claims. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (2) In this Part –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (a) ‘admiralty claim’ means a claim within the Admiralty jurisdiction of the High Court as set out in section 20 of the Senior Courts Act 1981 1 ;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (b) ‘the Admiralty Court’ means the Admiralty Court of the King’s Bench Division of the High Court of Justice;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (ba)“the Admiralty Judge” means the judge in charge of the Admiralty Court and any other judge authorised to sit in the Admiralty Court;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (bb)“the Admiralty Registrar” means the holder of the office of this name listed in column 1 of Part II of Schedule 2 to the Senior Courts Act 1981(1) or any person who is authorised to exercise the powers of this office in accordance with s.91(1) of the Act(2);

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (bc)“claim in personam” means an admiralty claim, other than a claim in rem, brought in accordance with section 21(1) of the Senior Courts Act 1981;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (c) ‘claim in rem’ means a claim in an admiralty action in rem brought in accordance with section 21(2) to (5) of the Senior Courts Act 1981;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (d) ‘collision claim’ means a claim within section 20(3)(b) of the Senior Courts Act 1981;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (e) ‘limitation claim’ means a claim under the Merchant Shipping Act 1995 2 for the limitation of liability in connection with a ship or other property;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (f) ‘salvage claim’ means a claim –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (i) for or in the nature of salvage;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (ii) for special compensation under Article 14 of Schedule 11 to the Merchant Shipping Act 1995;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (iii) for the apportionment of salvage; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (iv) arising out of or connected with any contract for salvage services;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (g) ‘caution against arrest’ means a caution entered in the Register under rule 61.7;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (h) ‘caution against release’ means a caution entered in the Register under rule 61.8;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (i) ‘the Register’ means the Register of cautions against arrest and release which is open to inspection as provided by Practice Direction 61;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (j) ‘the Marshal’ means the Admiralty Marshal;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (k) ‘ship’ includes any vessel used in navigation;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (l) ‘the Registrar’ means the Admiralty Registrar; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (m) ‘electronic track data’ means a digital or electronic recording of the track of a vessel (including any associated visual or aural recordings) as recorded by, for example, ship or shore-based AIS (Automatic Identification System), ECDIS (Electronic Chart and Display Information System), or a voyage data recorder

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (3) Part 58 (Commercial Court) applies to claims in the Admiralty Court except where this Part provides otherwise. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.1] (4) The Registrar has all the powers of the Admiralty judge except where a rule or practice direction provides otherwise. ## Admiralty claims

## 61.2

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (1) The following claims must be started in the Admiralty Court –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (a) a claim –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (i) in rem;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (ii) for damage done by a ship;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (iii) concerning the ownership of a ship;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (iv) under the Merchant Shipping Act 1995;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (v) Omitted

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (vi) by a master or member of a crew for wages;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (vii) in the nature of towage; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (viii) in the nature of pilotage;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (b) a collision claim;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (c) a limitation claim; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (d) a salvage claim. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (2) Any other admiralty claim may be started in the Admiralty Court and a claim for loss of life or personal injury specified in section 20(2)(f) of the Senior Courts Act 1981(1) should be started in the Admiralty Court in the circumstances set out in Practice Direction 61. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (3) Rule 30.5 applies to claims in the Admiralty Court except that the Admiralty Court may order the transfer of a claim to –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (a) the Commercial Court;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (b) a Circuit Commercial Court; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (c) Omitted

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.2] (d) any other appropriate court. ## Claims in rem

## 61.3

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.3] (1) This rule applies to claims in rem. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.3] (2) A claim in rem is started by the issue of an in rem claim form as set out in Practice Direction 61. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.3] (3) Subject to rule 61.4, the particulars of claim must –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.3] (a) be contained in or served with the claim form; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.3] (b) be served on the defendant by the claimant within 75 days after service of the claim form. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.3] (4) An acknowledgment of service must be filed within 14 days after service of the claim form. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.3] (5) The claim form must be served –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.3] (a) in accordance with Practice Direction 61; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.3] (b) within 12 months after the date of issue and rules 7.5 and 7.6 are modified accordingly. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.3] (6) If a claim form has been issued (whether served or not), any person who wishes to defend the claim may file an acknowledgment of service. ## Special provisions relating to collision claims

## 61.4

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (1) This rule applies to collision claims. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (2) A claim form should not contain or be followed by particulars of claim and rule 7.4 does not apply. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (3) An acknowledgment of service must be filed. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (4) A party who wishes to dispute the court’s jurisdiction must make an application under Part 11 within 2 months after filing his acknowledgment of service. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (4A) Every party must—

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (a) within 21 days after the defendant files their acknowledgment of service; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (b) where the defendant applies under Part 11, within 21 days after the defendant files their further acknowledgment of service,

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] disclose any electronic track data which is or has been in its control, in accordance with Part 31, and provide copies, or permit inspection, of that electronic track data within 7 days of a request by another party to do so. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (5) Every party must –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (a) within 2 months after the defendant files the acknowledgment of service; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (b) where the defendant applies under Part 11, within 2 months after the defendant files the further acknowledgment of service,

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] file at the court a completed collision statement of case in the form specified in Practice Direction 61. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (6) A collision statement of case must—

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (a) be in a form set out in Practice Direction 61

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (b) contain the matters set out in Practice Direction 61; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (c) be verified by a statement of truth. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (6A) Each party must file a collision defence in respect of each collision statement of case filed by another party. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (6B) A party’s collision defence must—

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (a) be filed within 28 days of service of the relevant collision statement of case on that party;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (b) comply with the requirements set out in Practice Direction 61; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (c) be verified by a statement of truth. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (6C) A party may file a collision reply to a collision defence filed by another party. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (6D) A party’s collision reply must—

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (a) be filed within 21 days of service of the relevant collision defence on that party; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (b) be verified by a statement of truth. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (7) A claim form in a collision claim in personam may not be served out of the jurisdiction unless; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (a) the case falls within section 22(2)(a), (b) or (c) of the Supreme Court Act 1981 3 ; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (b) the defendant has submitted to or agreed to submit to the jurisdiction; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] the court gives permission in accordance with Section IV of Part 6. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (c) rule 6.33 applies. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (8) Where permission to serve a claim form out of the jurisdiction is given, the court will specify the period within which the defendant may file an acknowledgment of service and, where appropriate, a collision statement of case. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (9) Where, in a collision claim in rem (‘the original claim’) –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (a)

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (i) a counterclaim; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (ii) a cross claim in rem

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] arising out of the same collision or occurrence is made; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (b)

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (i) the party bringing the original claim has caused the arrest of a ship or has obtained security in order to prevent such arrest; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (ii) the party bringing the counterclaim or cross claim is unable to arrest a ship or otherwise obtain security,

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] the party bringing the counterclaim or cross claim may apply to the court to stay the original claim until sufficient security is given to satisfy any judgment that may be given in favour of that party. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (10) The consequences set out in paragraph (11) apply where a party to a claim to establish liability for a collision claim (other than a claim for loss of life or personal injury) –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (a) makes an offer to settle in the form set out in paragraph (12) not less than 21 days before the start of the trial;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (b) that offer is not accepted; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (c) the maker of the offer obtains at trial an apportionment equal to or more favourable than his offer. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (11) Where paragraph (10) applies the parties will, unless the court considers it unjust, be entitled to the following costs –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (a) the maker of the offer will be entitled to –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (i) all his costs from 21 days after the offer was made; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (ii) his costs before then in accordance with the apportionment found at trial; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (b) all other parties to whom the offer was made –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (i) will be entitled to their costs up to 21 days after the offer was made in accordance with the apportionment found at trial; but

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (ii) will not be entitled to their costs thereafter. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (12) An offer under paragraph (10) must be in writing and must contain –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (a) an offer to settle liability at stated percentages;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (b) an offer to pay costs in accordance with the same percentages;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (c) a term that the offer remain open for 21 days after the date it is made; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.4] (d) a term that, unless the court orders otherwise, on expiry of that period the offer remains open on the same terms except that the offeree should pay all the costs from that date until acceptance. ## Arrest

## 61.5

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (1) In a claim in rem –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (a) a claimant; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (b) a judgment creditor

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] may apply to have the property proceeded against arrested. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (2) Practice Direction 61 sets out the procedure for applying for arrest. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (3) A party making an application for arrest must –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (a) request a search to be made in the Register before the warrant is issued to determine whether there is a caution against arrest in force with respect to that property; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (b) file a declaration in the form set out in Practice Direction 61. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (4) A warrant of arrest may not be issued as of right in the case of property in respect of which the beneficial ownership, as a result of a sale or disposal by any court in any jurisdiction exercising admiralty jurisdiction in rem, has changed since the claim form was issued. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (5) A warrant of arrest may not be issued against a ship owned by a State where by any convention or treaty, the United Kingdom has undertaken to minimise the possibility of arrest of ships of that State until –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (a) notice in the form set out in Practice Direction 61 has been served on a consular officer at the consular office of that State in London or the port at which it is intended to arrest the ship; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (b) a copy of that notice is attached to any declaration under paragraph (3)(b). [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (6) Except –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (a) with the permission of the court; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (b) where notice has been given under paragraph (5),

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] a warrant of arrest may not be issued in a claim in rem against a foreign ship belonging to a port of a State in respect of which an order in council has been made under section 4 of the Consular Relations Act 1968 4 , until the expiration of 2 weeks from appropriate notice to the consul. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (7) A warrant of arrest is valid for 12 months but may only be executed if the claim form –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (a) has been served; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (b) remains valid for service at the date of execution. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (8) Property may only be arrested by the Marshal or his substitute. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (9) Property under arrest –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (a) may not be moved unless the court orders otherwise; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (b) may be immobilised or prevented from sailing in such manner as the Marshal may consider appropriate. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.5] (10) Where an in rem claim form has been issued and security sought, any person who has filed an acknowledgment of service may apply for an order specifying the amount and form of security to be provided. ## Security in claim in rem

## 61.6

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.6] (1) This rule applies if, in a claim in rem, security has been given to –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.6] (a) obtain the release of property under arrest; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.6] (b) prevent the arrest of property. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.6] (2) Unless the terms on which security has been given provide otherwise, the court may order that—

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.6] (a )the amount of security be reduced, and may stay the claim until the order is complied with; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.6] (b) the amount of security be increased, and may give the claimant permission to arrest or re-arrest the property proceeded against to obtain further security

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.6] (3) The court may not make an order under paragraph (2)(b) if the total security to be provided would exceed the value of the property at the time –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.6] (a) of the original arrest; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.6] (b) security was first given (if the property was not arrested). ## Cautions against arrest

## 61.7

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.7] (1) Any person may file a request for a caution against arrest. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.7] (2) When a request under paragraph (1) is filed the court will enter the caution in the Register if the request is in the form set out in Practice Direction 61 and –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.7] (a) the person filing the request undertakes –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.7] (i) to file an acknowledgment of service; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.7] (ii) to give sufficient security to satisfy the claim with interest and costs; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.7] (b) where the person filing the request has constituted a limitation fund in accordance with Article 11 of the Convention on Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims 1976 5 he –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.7] (i) states that such a fund has been constituted; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.7] (ii) undertakes that the claimant will acknowledge service of the claim form by which any claim may be begun against the property described in the request. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.7] (3) A caution against arrest –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.7] (a) is valid for 12 months after the date it is entered in the Register; but

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.7] (b) may be renewed for a further 12 months by filing a further request. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.7] (4) Paragraphs (1) and (2) apply to a further request under paragraph (3)(b). [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.7] (5) Property may be arrested if a caution against arrest has been entered in the Register but the court may order that –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.7] (a) the arrest be discharged; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.7] (b) the party procuring the arrest pays compensation to the owner of or other persons interested in the arrested property. ## Release and cautions against release

## 61.8

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (1) Where property is under arrest –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (a) an in rem claim form may be served upon it; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (b) it may be arrested by any other person claiming to have an in rem claim against it. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (2) Any person who –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (a) claims to have an in rem right against any property under arrest; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (b) wishes to be given notice of any application in respect of that property or its proceeds of sale,

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] may file a request for a caution against release in the form set out in Practice Direction 61. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (3) When a request under paragraph (2) is filed, a caution against release will be entered in the Register. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (3A) A caution against release—

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (a) is valid for 12 months after the date it is entered in the Register; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (b) may be renewed for a further 12 months by filing a further request. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (4) Property will be released from arrest if –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (a) it is sold by the court;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (b) the court orders release on an application made by any party;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (c)

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (i) the arresting party; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (ii) all persons who have entered cautions against release

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] file a request for release in the form set out in Practice Direction 61; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (d) any party files –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (i) a request for release in the form set out in Practice Direction 61 (containing an undertaking); and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (ii) consents to the release of the arresting party and all persons who have entered cautions against release. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (5) Where the release of any property is delayed by the entry of a caution against release under this rule any person who has an interest in the property may apply for an order that the person who entered the caution pay damages for losses suffered by the applicant because of the delay. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (6) The court may not make an order under paragraph (5) if satisfied that there was good reason to –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (a) request the entry of; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (b) maintain

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] the caution. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (7) Any person –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (a) interested in property under arrest or in the proceeds of sale of such property; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (b) whose interests are affected by any order sought or made,

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] may be made a party to any claim in rem against the property or proceeds of sale. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (8) Where –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (a)

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (i) a ship is not under arrest but cargo on board her is; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (ii) a ship is under arrest but cargo on board her is not; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (b) persons interested in the ship or cargo wish to discharge the cargo,

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] they may, without being made parties, request the Marshal to authorise steps to discharge the cargo. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (9) If –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (a) the Marshal considers a request under paragraph (8) reasonable; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (b) the applicant gives an undertaking in writing acceptable to the Marshal to pay –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (i) his fees; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (ii) all expenses to be incurred by him or on his behalf

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] on demand,

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] the Marshal will apply to the court for an order to permit the discharge of the cargo. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (10) Where persons interested in the ship or cargo are unable or unwilling to give an undertaking as referred to in paragraph (9)(b), they may –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (a) be made parties to the claim; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (b) apply to the court for an order for –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (i) discharge of the cargo; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.8] (ii) directions as to the fees and expenses of the Marshal with regard to the discharge and storage of the cargo.
